heroCommands.comment: Run PyTorch in Docker with GPUs

sixtySeconds.whatItDoes: PyTorch is a Python library for deep learning. It provides tensors like NumPy arrays that run on GPUs, automatic differentiation, and building blocks for neural networks, and it's one of the most widely used frameworks for AI research and production.
sixtySeconds.problem: Training neural networks needs fast GPU maths and automatic gradients. PyTorch provides both with a Python-first, imperative style, so models are ordinary Python code you can debug line by line.
whoFor: Developers who need GPU-accelerated tensor maths
sixtySeconds.whyChoose: Choose it for flexibility and the huge ecosystem of models, tutorials and libraries built on it. For install commands for your exact OS and GPU, use the selector on pytorch.org.
requirements: An NVIDIA, AMD or Intel GPU for acceleration (optional)
For source builds: a C++20 compiler, 10 GB free disk and 30 to 60 minutes

overview: PyTorch is made of several components: torch, a tensor library with strong GPU support; torch.autograd, tape-based automatic differentiation; torch.nn, a neural network library built on autograd; torch.multiprocessing, with shared tensor memory across processes; and torch.utils, including DataLoader.

It is used either as a GPU-powered replacement for NumPy or as a flexible deep learning research platform. Networks are built dynamically, so you can change how a model behaves at runtime, and extensions can be written in Python or C++.

The README sends you to pytorch.org/get-started/locally for the pip and conda install commands for your system. It also documents pre-built Docker images, Jetson wheels and building from source with CUDA, ROCm or Intel GPU support. PyTorch has a BSD-style license.

install.verificationNote: Commands come from PyTorch's README. AIRepoHub hasn't run them yet.

steps.title: Get the command for your system
steps.body: The README says install commands for pip wheels and conda are on pytorch.org/get-started/locally. Choose your OS, package manager and compute platform there.

steps.title: Run the pre-built image
steps.body: Needs Docker 23.0+. --ipc=host gives enough shared memory for multi-worker data loading.

steps.title: Get the source
steps.code:
git clone https://github.com/pytorch/pytorch
cd pytorch
git submodule sync
git submodule update --init --recursive

steps.title: Install dependencies
steps.code:
pip install --group dev
pip install mkl-static mkl-include

steps.title: Build and install
steps.body: The first build takes 30 to 60 minutes.

troubleshooting.problem: Not sure which install command to use

troubleshooting.solution: Use gcc 11.3.0 or newer with full C++20 support, and make sure you have 10 GB free.
Install Visual Studio or the Visual C++ Build Tools; VS Code doesn't include them.
